Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing inquiry — expected monthly volume & peak TPS

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and the asks we agreed to: 

- Confirmed expected run-rate range: 35M–70M tokens / month (depends on rollout velocity).
- Average request size: ~1.2k tokens (mix of short prompts and longer context).
- Typical concurrency today is low, but expected peaks during batch scoring and synchronous user workflows. You estimated a 99th-percentile burst around ~75–90 TPS for 30–60s windows.
- Targeting hosted API for initial deployment; team will re-evaluate Dedicated if 99th spikes are sustained.

Immediate asks for us (per your ask):
1) Attach and share a sample usage export (you mentioned a CSV of last 30 days) so we can validate traffic shape and token distribution.
2) Confirm budget band: you suggested an internal cap of roughly $2k–$6k/mo for this first phase — can you confirm exact monthly dollar target per 1M tokens you expect us to price against?
3) Any hard SLOs around 99th latency for end-user RPCs?

I attached the hosted ratecard we discussed. I’ll loop in pricing for a quick sanity check once I have your CSV.

—Irene

Thanks Irene — appreciate the recap. CSV attached (last 30 days, anonymized IDs) — key notes:
- Median request tokens: 850
- Mean request tokens: 1,220
- Most heavy traffic between 09:30–11:00 PT and 16:00–17:00 PT, short spikes for ~45–90s
- Monthly extrapolated run-rate if rollout completes: ~52M tokens/month (we left the safety window to 35–70M)

Budget: we don’t have a formalized vendor budget yet. The execs said earlier they want to keep API spend below $5k/month initially and are hoping for a list price near $25–30 / 1M tokens. If that’s unrealistic we can discuss committed tiers.

SLOs: user-facing RPCs target 500ms p99 where possible; batch scoring can be slower (up to 2s p99 okay).

Let me know if you need any other exports.

Folks — forwarding Alex’s export and notes. Highlights we should evaluate for quick pricing guidance:

- Extrapolated run-rate ~52M tokens/mo (they’re comfortable with 35–70M window).
- Peaks: short 45–90s bursts hitting ~75–90 TPS; p99 RPC latency target 500ms.
- Prospect expects list price around $25–30 / 1M tokens; they want spend <$5k/mo initially unless committed discount changes economics.

Questions for you:
1) For hosted API, do we have a sensible list-price proposal that meets their latency needs in US region and keeps below $25–30 / 1M? (I think our current hosted list for this model is $40 / 1M.)
2) If we can’t hit $25–30 as-hosted, what committed slab would get them into $20 / 1M net? What commitment (tokens/mo or $/mo and term) needed?
3) Operational notes: should we recommend a small Dedicated trial for the 99th spikes or can routing + autoscaling + burst buffers in hosted keep them within 500ms p99 for short spikes?

I’ll have a short reply to Alex today with concrete bands. Please flag if you want to join a quick call with SignalVault next week.

—Irene

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 08:35:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API pricing inquiry — expected monthly volume & peak TPS

Irene / Jordan — quick pricing sanity check below. I ran a back-of-envelope using their numbers and our hosted economics for the model family they tested. Rough outputs: 

- Expected monthly tokens: use 52M as base (we should present a 35M / 52M / 70M tier set).
- Average tokens per request: 1.2k (matches their mean) => ~43k requests/day at 52M.
- Peak concurrency: 80 TPS / 90 TPS delta; given 45–90s spikes we can absorb with autoscaling + prefix caching.

Proposed public-facing bands (hosted API):
A) List: $40 / 1M tokens (no commit).
B) Small commit: $27 / 1M tokens net with a 6-month 30k-50k USDT (i.e., $810–$1350) monthly token commitment (equivalent slabs) — gets them near their $25–30 target.
C) Medium commit: $18 / 1M tokens net with 12-month commitment at 300k tokens/day average (approx $3,240/mo).

Notes on SLOs & ops: short bursts to 90 TPS can be handled by hosted if we configure burst capacity and add a soft concurrency limit with graceful 429+retry guidance. For a hard p99 500ms requirement during spikes, Dedicated simplifies the guarantee, but we should propose an initial hosted trial with a canary SLA clause and a follow-up Dedicated baseline if spikes become sustained.

Irene — I’ll draft an email to Alex with the three bands and a recommended next step: 30-day hosted pilot on band B (small commit) + optional dedicated POC if p99 violations exceed thresholds for more than 10% of days in the pilot.

Karthik
VP, Pricing & Revenue Operations
